title: Analytics Authorization Orchestrator: unified RBAC gateway for usage endpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, centralized authorization orchestrator for all console analytics endpoints and usage views. This service will: 1) normalize incoming analytics requests (route, auth token, tenant context), 2) consult entitlements and policy rules to produce query scopes and row/column-level masks, 3) emit an authorization decision token for downstream query runners and cached views, and 4) provide an audit trail for compliance. The orchestrator replaces ad-hoc checks in analytics services with a single, versioned decision point to improve consistency, simplify future access models (groups, org roles, feature entitlements), and enable fine-grained controls (columns, aggregated vs raw exports).
comments: 2025-02-10 - Initial ticket created by Maya; documented goals and high-level API shape. Linked to audit requirements from legal (Confluence: /display/INF/Analytics+Access+Controls).

2025-02-11 - Tech kickoff: decided to implement a local caching layer for entitlement checks (TTL 30s) to reduce p99 auth latency; Arjun prototyped a bench showing <3ms median extra latency with cache enabled. Trade-off: shorter TTL increases load on entitlement-syncer but lowers staleness.

2025-02-12 - Security review feedback: require signed decision tokens with rotation via KMS; added explicit requirement for audit logging of denied queries. Security suggested OPA or a ruleset-compatible evaluator — team opted for a minimal rules evaluator first, with OPA adapter planned for phase 2. Action: open PR for token format spec.

2025-02-13 - PM (Clara Torres) asked for migration plan for existing endpoints. Decided on a staged rollout: 1) opt-in routing for internal analytics consumers (console-readonly), 2) canary for 5% external console traffic, 3) rollout after 72h stability. Added instrumentation hooks for per-route auth latency and denial rate.
2025-02-14 - Design/UX: agreed on error surfaces for end-users (403 with trace id and help link) vs engineers (detailed audit id). Created a small doc with UX samples (Drive: /r/console-auth-errors).
2025-02-15 - Integration note: deferred column-level masking for exports v1 due to time; will block export endpoints behind a stricter allowlist and handle masking in the exporter service for now.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization orchestrator service deployed behind feature flag and reachable from console analytics API gateway.
All decisions are mutable by policy version; decision tokens are signed and verifiable by downstream services.
Per-route and per-tenant denial rates and authz latency are collected into Grafana dashboards; p99 auth latency < 30ms in canary under typical load.
Backwards-compatible migration path exists: endpoints can fallback to existing in-service checks when orchestrator is disabled.
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) exist for allow, deny, and masked responses; PRs and test run IDs are linked in PRs.
